name: Lienzer Altstadt
kurzbeschreibung: The historic old town of Lienz enchants visitors as the sun-drenched heart of East Tyrol with Mediterranean flair, colourful townhouses, and the striking Liebburg.
tags: Leinz (or 'Lienz' if referring to the city)
beschreibung:
Overview

The enchanting Old Town of Lienz is considered the vibrant cultural and social heart of East Tyrol. Nestled in a sunny basin at the confluence of the Isel and Drau rivers, framed by the rugged limestone peaks of the Lienz Dolomites, the district capital exudes an almost Mediterranean atmosphere. The focal point of local life is the spacious Hauptplatz, dominated by the imposing Liebburg, a splendid 17th-century palace that serves today as the town hall. Colourful townhouses with historic facades, flower-decked balconies, shady pavement cafes, and traditional craft boutiques give the pedestrian zone an unmistakable charm, effortlessly blending alpine heritage with southern warmth.

Route & Requirements

A stroll through the historic town centre is a pleasure for visitors of all generations and requires no hiking gear or athletic conditioning. The pedestrian area is largely flat, paved with smooth stones, and fully accessible for wheelchair users and strollers. A classic walking circuit leads from Johannesplatz through charming Rosengasse to Hauptplatz, continuing to the historic Spitalskirche with its delicate Gothic murals, and along the picturesque Isel riverside promenade. Those seeking broader vistas can take a gentle uphill walk toward the Schlossberg to visit the medieval castle of Schloss Bruck.

Visiting & Getting There

Lienz enjoys excellent rail and road connections. Lienz railway station on the Drau Valley Railway line is situated only a few minutes' walk from the pedestrian centre, offering frequent train and bus services connecting to Carinthia, South Tyrol, and northern Tyrol. Motorists arrive via the B100 Drautalstraße or the B108 Felbertauern route. Several designated parking areas and multi-storey garages are located adjacent to the historic centre, including the Dolomitencenter car park. The old town is open and free to explore year-round. A special highlight is the weekly Lienz farmers' market on Fridays and Saturdays, offering delicious regional specialities directly from mountain farms.

Tips

Pause at one of the sunny outdoor cafes on Hauptplatz to sample authentic East Tyrolean Schlipfkrapfen dumplings or homemade ice cream. During winter, the square before the Liebburg hosts one of the most atmospheric Advent markets in the Alps, transforming the palace facade into a giant illuminated calendar. Art lovers should not miss Schloss Bruck, which houses the world's most significant collection of works by master painter Albin Egger-Lienz.
